description:
Kids First Electric Scooter: The 5TH WHEEL K1 will be a fantastic gift for your little explorer. With front shock for added stability and safety, the scooter also features soft and comfortable PP handles that not only protect your child's hands but also provide a non-slip, enhancing their control and riding experience. Suitable for children aged 6 and above, the aluminum frame is a reliable choice, supporting a maximum weight of 110 lbs.

Guarding Playful Moments: Our Kid's electric scooter comes equipped with a robust 150W motor, delivering powerful performance and a top speed of up to 9.3 mph. With each charge, it offers a riding range of 5 miles (depending on weight and terrain). Incorporating 6.5 inch rubber tires, it offers superior terrain adaptability, ensuring a smooth ride across various riding scenarios.

Easy Setup and Safety: Your child can easily master the use of this electric scooter. Control your speed with the thumb throttle on the right handle, while the left handle features an EABS brake. Plus, there's a foot brake for immediate stops in any situation, ensuring safety.

Portable and Upright Design: Our scooter features a one-button folding mechanism and a upright option, a rare design in the market. It can stand upright without the need for a kickstand, making storage effortless and space-saving.

24 Hours Customer Service: 5TH WHEEL provides 100% compensation for product problems, 12-month warranty & 24/7 online customer service. We value all customers in our store, if you have any questions, please feel free to reach us anytime.

K1 Kids Electric Kick Scooter

The colors of the electric scooter are suitable as a gift for a boy or a girl.

150W powerful motor can output stable power and allows load capacity up to 110 lbs.
Large capacity battery makes the scooter max range up to 5 Miles and 2-3 hours full charge quickly
The deck uses non-slip material, easy and comfortable for your kid to stand on.

The handle uses non-slip rubber material, easy and comfortable for your kid to hold.
